beginner.headline: Kyiv Bridge Hit by Drone; German Chancellor Visits
beginner.brief: A bridge in Kyiv was hit by a Russian drone. Vehicles were moving on the bridge when it was hit. The drone attack created a large fireball and black smoke. Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by drones for four days. Two people were injured in the latest attack. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Kyiv to show support. He met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The damaged bridges are still standing, but traffic is difficult.

intermediate.headline: Kyiv Bridges Targeted in Aerial Vehicle Attacks Amidst German Chancellor's Visit
intermediate.brief: Major bridges in Kyiv have been affected by Russian aerial vehicle strikes for four consecutive days. Two people were injured after the Pivnichnyi Bridge was struck on Sunday morning. This recent assault occurred during German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's unexpected journey to Kyiv. Russia's military announced it would increase attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions. Video recordings of Sunday's incident showed cars on Pivnichnyi Bridge when an aerial vehicle crashed into it, creating an explosion. Other videos showed a noticeable opening in a traffic lane on the bridge. The two impacted bridges are still standing, but damage has caused significant traffic problems in parts of the capital. While emergency services worked on the incidents, Germany's Merz held a meeting with President Zelensky in Kyiv.

advanced.headline: Kyiv Bridges Targeted in Drone Attacks as German Chancellor Visits
advanced.brief: The latest Russian unmanned aerial vehicle attack on Kyiv's Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge coincided with a surprise visit from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to the Ukrainian capital. Video footage, independently verified, captured the moment an unmanned aerial vehicle crashed into the Pivnichyi Bridge as traffic moved across it, resulting in a large conflagration and a rising cloud of black smoke. This attack marked the fourth successive day that major bridges in Kyiv have been targeted by Russian aerial assaults, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital. Two individuals sustained non-fatal injuries when the Pivnichyi Bridge was struck for the second day in a row, with the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge also having been targeted multiple times earlier in the week. Other social media content showed a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge, evidencing significant structural damage. Kyiv's eight bridges spanning the Dnipro River are essential arteries, linking the city's eastern and western sectors, with many of the capital's estimated three million inhabitants relying heavily on public transport and personal vehicles for daily transit. Although the two targeted bridges remain structurally sound, the damage and subsequent traffic restrictions have at times led to widespread gridlock across parts of the capital. A Kyiv resident conveyed the severity of the travel disruption, stating, "'To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell.'" Repair teams are actively addressing the damage, and officials are exploring contingency measures like temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services, and even a river tunnel to ensure Kyiv remains connected. Beyond the bridge attacks, other Russian aerial bombardments on Sunday damaged a heating main, causing a temporary hot water shortage in the Desnyanskyi district. Additionally, Russian drones struck a warehouse in Sumy, claiming one life, as reported by President Zelensky. Ukraine's Air Force reported that out of 135 unmanned aerial vehicles launched overnight by Russia, including 52 jet-powered variants, 125 projectiles were successfully intercepted. As emergency services responded, German Chancellor Merz met President Zelensky in Kyiv, and they laid wreaths for Ukrainian soldiers killed in the war. Merz reaffirmed Germany's support for Ukraine, stating, "'Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.'" Merz underscored Germany's position, asserting, "'Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well.'" Since Merz assumed the chancellorship in May 2025, Germany has become Ukraine's single largest financial benefactor. President Zelensky has consistently appealed to Western allies for more sophisticated military assistance, specifically requesting advanced interceptors capable of shooting down newer jet-powered Russian unmanned aerial vehicles and ballistic missiles. Russia's defense ministry declared its intention to intensify its campaign across Ukraine, framing it as a response to Zelensky's earlier remarks about escalating attacks on Russian oil refineries. The Russian foreign ministry reiterated a warning for foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv. Responding to this warning, EU ambassador Katarína Mathernová declared, "'The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!'" German ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, echoed this sentiment, stating, "'Amen - we're staying'." Experts assess that while Russian aerial assaults are unlikely to demolish the bridges outright, sustained targeting risks forcing their closure and weakening their structural integrity, ultimately rendering them unusable.
